note: MOST BEAUTIFUL PUBS: pubs worth visiting for the room or the building - interiors, exteriors and a few views. Collected 14 Sep 2026. Built as its own guide beside historic-pubs-dining-rooms-london (Claude's call on the config's open question, option a): some headline venues are shared, as they are across food topics, and the design-award and one-off-design material is the difference. Common names carry the area: Red Lion, Duke of York Street is the three-star gin palace; The George is Great Portland Street (CAMRA 2023 refurbishment); The George Inn is Borough. TIER E: Reddit cannot be read here; a r/london thread 'What is the most beautiful pub in London?' (11egyx3) surfaced in search.

sources.name: CAMRA - National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors and Pub Design Awards
sources.note: ONE SOURCE, TWO CAMRA PROGRAMMES ON ONE DOMAIN (distinct-domains rule). (1) The National Inventory, a judged register of interiors, read from camra.org.uk/heritage-pubs/national-inventory on 14 Sep 2026: London's three-star (60) and two-star (62) entries are recorded; the 147 one-star London entries ('some national historic importance') are not, because a one-star rating is about surviving fabric rather than a room worth travelling to see. The config recorded this register as dead because heritagepubs.org.uk now redirects to a gambling site; it moved to camra.org.uk. (2) The Pub Design Awards, run with Historic England, read year by year at camra.org.uk/awards/pub-design?selected_year=<year> in the browser (the year switcher is client-rendered): London results for 2022-2026 only. National awards, scoped to London (trap 12).

sources.name: Nuff - The most beautiful pubs in London
sources.note: Undated. East and north London heavy. 'Every one is picked by us, locals who actually drink in them and pay for the pints... we're mostly in it for the fabric of the place.'
